question:
A 23-year-old male presents to the emergency department following a knife altercation. The
examination reveals a severed common digital nerve to the index finger of his dominant hand, with an
8mm gap between the nerve endings. When discussing treatment options with this patient, which of the
following repair methods has been shown to be equivalent in efficacy to autologous nerve grafting?
Answer Choices: (A) Direct nerve transfer (B) Polyglycolic acid conduit (C) Synthetic nerve scaffold (D)
Silicone tube conduit (E) Tension-based repair with flexed positioning (F) Primary end-to-end repair (G)
Collagen conduit (H) Vein graft conduit (I) Processed allograft nerve (J) Fibrin glue repair
 A. Collagen conduit
B. Silicone tube conduit
C. Processed allograft nerve
D. Polyglycolic acid conduit
E. Tension-based repair with flexed positioning
F. Fibrin glue repair
G. Synthetic nerve scaffold
H. Primary end-to-end repair
I. Vein graft conduit
J. Direct nerve transfer
